# 0x226 — `rider_settings`

DLC 7 · 100 Hz · status: **confirmed**

The settings the rider makes in the dash menu, sent continuously: riding mode, traction-control mode and level, two further assist levels (SCS and LIF, which is which is open), the quickshifter enables and the brake-control mode. The frame changes only when the rider changes a setting.

## Layout

Bytes are numbered from 0. Multi-byte values are big-endian unless a row says otherwise. Bit 7 is the most significant bit of a byte.

| Byte | Content |
|---|---|
| B0 | `ride_mode`, `tcs_level`, `assist_level_a` |
| B1 | `qs_down_enabled` |
| B2 | — |
| B3 | `tcs_mode` |
| B4 | — |
| B5 | `bc_mode`, `assist_level_b`, `qs_up_enabled` |
| B6 | — |

| `ride_mode` | B0 bits 7..6 | 2-bit field | enum |  | confirmed (medium) |

### `ride_mode`

Riding mode (see 0x209 `ride_mode`). This frame changes first; 0x209 follows 10-20 ms later.

| Raw | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | D-MODE 1 |
| 1 | D-MODE 2 |
| 2 | D-MODE 3 |
| 3 | D-MODE 4 |

**Confirmed by:** The dash on video with spoken markers.

**How we know:** The rider stepped through the four modes with the dash in the frame; this field followed each step. Repeated twice on a later ride.

**Example:** `0x226  0F 01 00 03 00 2D 00` → 0

### `tcs_level`

Traction-control level in effect. In the TCS 1 and TCS 2 modes it equals the mode; in M it is the level the rider set inside M. 0x209 B3 bits 4..1 and 0x215 B6 bits 2..1 copy this field.

| Raw | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | probably TCS OFF (not confirmed) |
| 1 | TCS level 1 |
| 2 | TCS level 2 |
| 3 | TCS level 3 |

**Confirmed by:** The dash on video for the TCS 1 and TCS 2 modes; the rider's own M setup (TCS 2, later raised to 3).

**How we know:** On a day when the rider's M setup had TCS level 2, the dash showed M, `tcs_mode` read 3 and this field read 2; when the rider raised the level to 3 inside M, B0 went 0x0B -> 0x0F and the 0x209 copy followed 10 ms later. In the presets it equals the mode shown on the dash at every filmed change.

**Example:** `0x226  0B 01 00 03 00 26 00` → 2

### `assist_level_a`

The SCS (slide control) or LIF (lift control) level, 1-3; which of the two is not known. 1 in the TCS 1 mode, 2 in TCS 2, 3 in the rider's M setup. The other one is `assist_level_b`.

| Raw | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | level 1 |
| 2 | level 2 |
| 3 | level 3 |

**Example:** `0x226  0B 01 00 03 00 26 00` → 3

### `tcs_pattern`

An earlier reading of the low nibble of B0 as the TCS level written twice (0x5 = TCS 1, 0xA = TCS 2, 0xF = M). It is two fields, `tcs_level` and `assist_level_a`; 0x5 and 0xA are the two presets, and in M the nibble is whatever the rider set (0xB with TCS 2 and the assist at 3, 0xF with everything at 3).

### `qs_down_enabled`

Quickshifter DOWN enabled, the rider's menu setting. The rest of B1 is always 0.

| Raw | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | off |
| 1 | on |

**Confirmed by:** The dash on video while the rider switched the setting in the menu.

**How we know:** Switched OFF and back ON in the menu with the dash filmed: the bit followed both within 25 ms of the dash. 1 on every other recording, where the setting was on.

**Example:** `0x226  0F 01 00 03 00 2D 00` → 1

### `tcs_mode`

Traction-control mode as the dash shows it. Levels 1 and 2 can be switched while riding with the throttle closed; M can be entered or left only at a standstill, and the captures agree: every change into or out of M happened at 0 km/h. The level in effect is `tcs_level`, which differs from this field in M.

| Raw | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | probably TCS OFF (not confirmed) |
| 1 | TCS 1 |
| 2 | TCS 2 |
| 3 | TCS M (manual) |

**Confirmed by:** The dash on video with spoken markers.

**How we know:** 12 changes of mode and TCS level in one filmed session, each matched to the value on the dash; 13 TCS changes across all early sessions. A later filmed session: 9 of 9 changes within 61 ms of the dash, and 22 more changes on that day, all at a standstill.

**Caveats:** Once, inside M, this byte went 3 -> 2 -> 3 for 2 s while the rest of the frame and 0x209 stayed put. Not explained.

**Example:** `0x226  0B 01 00 03 00 26 00` → 3

### `tcs_level_b5`

An earlier reading of B5 as 0x20 + TCS level × 4 + `bc_mode`, with bit 5 always set. It fitted every frame of the early rides because the presets were in use, or M with every level at 3, and the quickshifter was always on. Bits 3..2 are `assist_level_b`, bit 5 is `qs_up_enabled`.

### `bc_mode`

Brake control (BC) mode. The ABS unit repeats it in 0x268 B4 bits 4..3, about 20 ms later. The field changes when a choice is accepted in the menu, not while it is only highlighted.

| Raw | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | BC1 |
| 2 | BC2 |

**Confirmed by:** The dash on video while the rider switched BC1 and BC2 in the menu.

**How we know:** BC2 -> BC1 -> BC2 in the menu with the dash filmed: the field went 2 -> 1 -> 2 within 60 ms of each accept. Equal to 0x268 B4 bits 4..3 in 414 370 of 414 370 paired frames of the earlier rides. It read 1 in every capture up to 2026-07 and 2 in every one from 2026-09, which matches the rider's own setting (BC2 since the summer).

**Example:** `0x226  0F 01 00 03 00 2D 00` → 1

### `assist_level_b`

The other of SCS and LIF, level 1-3 (see `assist_level_a`). 1 in the TCS 1 mode, 2 in TCS 2, 1 in the rider's M setup and 3 after an edit inside M that changed nothing else. 0x215 B5 bits 1..0 copy it.

| Raw | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 1 | level 1 |
| 2 | level 2 |
| 3 | level 3 |

**Example:** `0x226  0B 01 00 03 00 26 00` → 1

### `qs_up_enabled`

Quickshifter UP enabled, the rider's menu setting.

| Raw | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | off |
| 1 | on |

**Confirmed by:** The dash on video while the rider switched the setting in the menu.

**How we know:** Switched OFF and back ON in the menu with the dash filmed: the bit followed both within 50 ms of the dash. 1 on every other recording, where the setting was on.

**Example:** `0x226  0F 01 00 03 00 2D 00` → 1

> The very first frame after power-on reads `05 01 00 01 00 25 28` whatever the real settings; the real values follow within 10 ms.

> B2 and B4 are always 0x00, and so are the bits of B1 and B5 not listed here. B6 is 0x00 in normal frames.

> In the TCS 1 and TCS 2 modes all three levels (`tcs_level`, `assist_level_a`, `assist_level_b`) equal the mode: B0 low nibble 0x5 and B5 0x26 in TCS 1, 0xA and 0x2A in TCS 2 (with BC2 and both quickshifter directions on). In M each level is whatever the rider set.
